page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is an entry-level virtual private server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel x86_64 core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is allocated on a shared basis. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 128 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is average at 1873.78, and the Geekbench single-core score reaches 1456.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3596.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2405.0, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is constrained, showing poor uncached read and write speeds of 22.81 GB/sec and 12.89 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression is a notable strength, processing at 32.63 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU architecture and low memory capacity, this server is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core execution or high memory throughput. Database operations and Redis SET performance are poor, making it less suitable for heavy database hosting. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, development environments, and simple background processes where cost efficiency is prioritized over high-performance multi-core scaling.
